full_judgment:
Sirajul Islam J: This Rule under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, at the instance of defendant No.2 was directed against the judgment and decree dated 13-6-1994 and 29-6-1994 respectively passed by Addl. Dist. Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.315 of 1993 affirming the judgment and decree dated 21-8-1993 and 28-8-1993 respectively passed by Assistant Judge, 5th Addl. Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.90 of 1992 decreeing the suit for eviction of the petitioner from the suit property. 

 4. After trial of the case, the learned Assistant Judge, decreed the suit for eviction against the defendants by his judgment and decree dated 21-8-1993 and 28-8-1993 respectively. Against this judgment and decree the defendant No.2 preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No.315 of 1993 which was heard by the Additional District Judge 2nd Court, Dhaka. The learned Additional District Judge after considering the facts, circumstances and the evidences of the case, dismissed the appeal and confirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court vide his judgment and decree dated 13-6-1994 and 29-6-94 respectively. 

 5. Being aggrieved by this judgment and decree passed by the learned Additional District Judge, the defendant No.2 Commander (Retd) A A Chowdhury, as a petitioner, has filed this revisional application in this court and obtained the present Rule. 

 6. It appears that admittedly the plaintiffs are the owners of the suit premises. It is also an admitted fact that the defendant No.1 was the tenant in the suit premises under the plaintiffs on the basis of two different written agreements, one after the other for a period of 5 years each. The plaintiffs case is, that the period of 2nd agreement of tenancy (Ext.1) for second 5 years starting from 1-3-1986 at a rent of Taka 8000.00 per month expired on 1-3-1991. but that the defendant No.1 did not vacate the suit premises as per terms of agreement and so the plaintiffs filed the suit after service of notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act. It appears that the defendant No.1 did not contest the suit. The defendant No.2 only contested the suit. Both the learned courts below found that defendant No.2 as an illegal and unauthorised occupant in the suit premises and decreed the suit against both the defendants for eviction and for recovery of arrear rents from defendant No.2 by the impugned judgment and decree. 

 7. Mr. SR Paul, the learned senior Counsel with Mr. HR Sharif, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant No.2 petitioner, submitted that there was no prayer in the plaint for recovery of arrear rent and, as such, the learned courts below have committed an error of law and of fact in passing the decree for recovery of arrear rent. The learned Counsel argued that the court cannot grant any relief which has not been specifically asked for in the plaint and, as such, this part of the decree is not sustainable in law. In this connection, the learned Counsel referred to Order 7 rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure and said that the court cannot grant any relief which has not been specifically stated in the plaint. For better appreciation Order 7, rule 7 CPC is quoted below: 

 9. By a perusal of the order passed by the learned trial Court it appears that after discussing all the facts and evidences of the case consistent with the plaintiffs pleadings the learned trial Court came to the conclusion that the plaintiffs, under the rule of equity, should not be deprived of the fruits of their suit and thus the learned court found it just for the plaintiff to get the arrear rent @ Tk. 8,000/- per month for the unpaid period and with this finding of justness the court granted this as other relief which has been upheld by the learned Additional District Judge in appeal after discussing the evidence of the case more elaborately in the impugned judgment and decree. In the facts and circumstances of the case, we do not find anything wrong in this order as passed by the courts below for the purpose of giving full relief as the court thought just and proper under law and equity as per evidence of the case. 

 In that case the plaintiff prayed for declaration of his right of distribution, exhibition, exploitation, etc. of a dupe negative of a Bengali Film "Chandranath" and for a mandatory injunction directing the defendant to deliver the dupe negative of the film to the plaintiffs. The learned court granted a decree for recovery of possession of the dupe negative print instead of mandatory injunction. Their Lordships observed at para 66 at page 340 that Order 7 rule 7 CPC permits the grant of such general or other relief as may be thought by the court to be just although such relief has not been specifically asked for. 

 14. In has been contended by the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioner that since the defendant No. 2 has been found to be a tresspasser in the suit premises, a notice should have been served upon him under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act but since that has not been done, the decree for eviction as passed by the learned courts below against him is not sustainable in law. To counter this contention, Mr. Wahidul Momin Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite party referred to a number of decisions in the case of Md. Amir Ali and another vs. Abdul Mannan having died his heirs and legal representatives Abdur Rahim and others reported in 9 DLR 102, the case of Taherunnessa and others vs. Mrs. Nazma Begum and others reported in 40 DLR (AD) 36. The common principle as laid down in those decisions is that a sub-tenant has no right to stay in the suit premises and no notice to quit is necessary as against him and that when the tenancy itself was terminated a sub-lease in favour of defendant No. 2 cannot be said to have subsisted and no notice to the sub-lessee is required." We find that the defendant No. 1 in violation of terms of his written agreement inducted defendant No. 2 as sub-lessee and when his own tenancy was terminated on its expiry on 1-3-1991, the question of defendant 2's stay in the suit pemises or of notice to him does not arise. Thus we find that the contention as put forward on behalf of defendant No. 2 petitioner for notice has no substance. 

 16. It has been argued on behalf of the defendant No.2 that the decree for arrear rent as passed by the courts below is a decree for an unspecified amount of money and, as such, it is not tenable in law. But it appears from the impugned judgment as passed by the learned Additional District Judge that he has passed the decree for arrear rent @ Taka 8,000.00 per month from 1-4-1991 till the date of vacating the suit premises by the defendant No. 2. So, it is clearly a specified amount of Taka 8,000.00 multiplied by the number of the months of occupation for which amount the plaintiff shall pay the requisite court-fee as ordered in the impugned judgment passed by the learned Additional District Judge. 

 17. Considering all the facts, circumstance and the provisions of law as discussed above, we find that the learned Additional District Judge has not committed any error of law or of facts or procedure in passing the impugned judgment and decree. The impugned judgment, therefore dose not call for any interference by this court.
